benchmark.heatmap.lead.message: Geometric mean of the median ratios over the phase metrics: ×1.34 — 34 % slower on average, ×0.80 — 20 % faster. Under the number — how many metrics are significantly worse (▲) and better (▼) out of all comparable ones. Colour only when the difference is above 5 % and backed by significance. benchmark.traces.lead.message: JS heap, DOM nodes and event listeners over the whole form scenario — one line per participant. Phases are aligned: a phase measurement window is a band as wide as the slowest participant, and between the bands is a gap without measurement (pauses, checks, garbage collection). Hover a chart or press ←/→ — the tooltip shows every participant’s values at that moment.

benchmark.traces.legendHint.message: hover a name to highlight its line

benchmark.traces.missing.message: No traces for this form — the values are in the tables of the “All phases” section.

benchmark.traces.aria.message: Trace charts: {form}. Left and right arrows move the cursor, Shift — by 10 steps, Home and End — to the edges, Esc — hide; plus and minus — zoom, 0 — the whole trace.

benchmark.traces.zoom.state.message: ×{k} · {where} · double-click a chart for the whole trace

benchmark.traces.zoom.hint.message: Drag over a stretch or click a phase number to zoom in; Ctrl/⌘ + wheel — zoom

benchmark.traces.source.message: The charts are a single traced pass per participant from a separate run {traceRun} on the same page build (git {sha}, built {date}), CPU {cpu}x: not a median but the shape of the curve. The table numbers are medians of run {run}.

benchmark.traces.sourceSame.message: The charts are a single traced pass per participant from run {run}, CPU {cpu}x: not a median but the shape of the curve. Exact numbers are in the tables of the “All phases” section.

benchmark.traces.garbage.message: The counters are shown without forced garbage collection: an unmounted form stays in the heap, DOM nodes and listeners until GC collects it — hence the sawtooth and the peaks, which do not mean a leak. Values after GC are in the phase tables.

benchmark.traces.warmupHidden.message: The warm-up before the remount is not shown on the charts. It is dozens of form mounts and unmounts in a row without measuring: the engine warms up the code (compiles and optimizes functions), and unmounted forms pile up in memory until it collects them — the line creeps up and looks like a leak, although after garbage collection everything returns to the initial level. The remount window starts after the warm-up and a forced garbage collection.

benchmark.traces.sourceOtherBuild.message: ⚠️ The charts are a single traced pass per participant from run {traceRun} on a different page build (git {sha}, built {date}), CPU {cpu}x; the table numbers are medians of run {run}. The forms may have changed between builds.

benchmark.traces.stale.message: ⚠️ The traces were recorded for the previous report — the table numbers on this page are newer.

benchmark.traces.unmarked.message: No phase marks in the trace (not shown): {list}.

benchmark.traces.table.message: Table: peak and end of the trace

benchmark.losses.lead.message: The report publishes everything, losses included. Below is every row where a competitor is significantly faster than ReFormer core (▼ in the full report), from the largest gap to the smallest.

benchmark.losses.summary.message: There are {n} such rows out of {total}. Who is ahead (a row can have several): {list}.

benchmark.phases.lead.message: A cell is the median over {runs} runs at CPU {cpu}x (each run is reduced first: for example, the median latency over all keys of the phase); below it is the q25–q75 spread. ×1.44 means 1.44 times worse than the best in the row; the best is in bold. Lower is better.

benchmark.phases.coreBest.message: ReFormer core is the best in {n} of {total}

benchmark.phases.apiCalls.message: API requests during the phase differ (part of the work moved to another phase): {list}.

benchmark.phases.failures.message: ⚠️ Failed runs: {n} — they are not included in the statistics.

benchmark.renders.lead.message: Components rendered during the phase (commits in parentheses); for typing — per key, for remounting — per mount. Counted by a DevTools hook (the PerformedWork flag, like React DevTools) in a separate pass at CPU 1x.

benchmark.bundle.lead.message: A separate production build of every page, the static closure of the entry. The main number is gzip over the baseline: how much the form library and the form code add to the same page without a library. Compression is measured on the whole entry; package attribution is minified bytes from the sourcemap.

benchmark.code.lead.message: Implementation sources that end up in the page bundle (from the sourcemap): lines without blanks and comments after prettier. “Form” is the files of the form folder, “glue” is the rest of the library integration code (field adapters, the RJSF theme, shared ReFormer rules and behavior). The shared benchmark layer is identical for everyone and is not counted. The credit JSON document of ReFormer JSON was generated once from shared field metadata; RJSF and ReFormer core build their schemas from the same metadata in code.

benchmark.method.contract.text.message: One specification per form; shared UI, fake API and messages for everyone. Competitors are written idiomatically from their official docs, without relying on ReFormer code, with the same optimization budget: no React Compiler and no manual memo beyond what the docs recommend.

benchmark.method.conformance.text.message: Before measuring, Playwright runs 171 tests: conformance of every implementation — errors and the quiet phase, server checks, masks, the wizard, arrays, the canonical payload — and the calibration of the render counter. Measuring starts only after a green run.

benchmark.method.stats.text.message: Each run is reduced first (for example, the median over all keys of a phase); over {runs} runs — the median and IQR. Significance against ReFormer core is an exact Mann–Whitney U test with the Holm correction over all comparisons of the report, p < 0.05; a difference below the A/A noise (two identical builds of ReFormer core) is not counted as a difference.

benchmark.method.health.text.message: At the start and the end of every run there is a calibration JS workload (machine speed drift) and a snapshot of neighbouring processes and the GPU; with BENCH_REQUIRE_IDLE=1 measuring does not start on a busy machine.

benchmark.method.drift.text.message: Absolute numbers from different sessions are not comparable even on the same machine: the baseline (the same code) differed by up to 1.6× between runs on one day. Compare ratios within one report: participants alternate in a shuffled order within a run, so drift affects everyone equally.

benchmark.method.limits.text.message: CPU throttling in Chromium slows down only the main thread, so the cost of large bundles is understated. One machine and one browser. “Key → end of frame” is quantized by the frame rate; “key → end of processing” and JS per key are more precise.

benchmark.method.link.report.message: the full report of this run

benchmark.method.link.libs.message: implementations of all participants; each README lists its deviations

benchmark.method.noHealth.message: The published report was taken before calibration and the background-load detector existed: machine speed drift and neighbouring processes were not measured in these runs.

benchmark.frameworks.hero.title.message: ReFormer in React, Vue and Angular

benchmark.frameworks.hero.lead.message: The same forms — registration with a captcha and a six-step credit application — from one JSON document with shared rules, behaviour and API, drawn by the ReFormer renderer of each framework and a component library. The measurement scenarios are those of the form-library report: load, typing, clicks, the wizard, arrays and remount.

benchmark.frameworks.fact.parity.message: same behaviour: {b} cross-e2e scenarios on the same builds before measuring

benchmark.frameworks.fact.noRank.message: {b}: median and spread, no “best” and no significance

benchmark.frameworks.results.lead.message: Key metrics of each form: the bar is the median over {runs} runs, the whisker is the interquartile range. Lower is better. There is no “best” mark and no significance: the stacks differ not only in the framework but also in the component library, so a difference in the numbers is about the whole stack.

benchmark.frameworks.phases.lead.message: A cell is the median over {runs} runs at CPU {cpu}x (each run is reduced first: for example, the median latency over all keys of the phase), below it is the q25–q75 spread. Lower is better. The JS (CDP) rows understate Vue — see the methodology. Expand a phase to see the charts.

benchmark.frameworks.traces.lead.message: JS heap, DOM nodes and event listeners over the whole form scenario — one line per stack. Phases are aligned: a phase's measurement window is a band as wide as the slowest stack, and between the bands is a gap without measurement. Hover the chart or press ←/→ — the tooltip shows every stack's values at that moment. The DOM node count depends on the component library's markup.

benchmark.frameworks.bundle.lead.message: A separate prod build of each page, the static closure from the page's modules. The bundle is the whole page: the framework, the component library, the renderer, the ReFormer core and the form code. The registry registers the whole component library — as an app on the JSON renderer does. Compression is computed for the whole entry; package attribution is minified bytes by sourcemap.

benchmark.frameworks.bundle.router.message: “Form: shared code” is the form document, rules, behaviour and fake API, the same on the three stacks. @angular/router in the Angular page's bundle comes with @taiga-ui/core (dialog portals); the page itself does not use the router. React and Vue are built by Vite (Rollup), Angular by the Angular CLI (esbuild).

benchmark.frameworks.code.lead.message: The code an app writes — the sources that end up in the page bundle (by sourcemap): lines without blanks and comments after prettier. “Form” is shared by the three stacks: the JSON document, rules, behaviour and API. “Stack glue” is each stack's own: the component library registry, the page entry and the app's components (captcha, computed value). The code of the component libraries and renderers is packages and is not counted.

benchmark.frameworks.method.stack.text.message: A participant is ReFormer, the framework and the component library together: React with @reformer/ui-kit, Vue with Vuetify, Angular with Taiga UI. The libraries draw fields differently — their own markup, styles, pop-up lists — so the numbers are about the stack, not the framework alone, and they do not isolate the cost of the ReFormer renderer.

benchmark.frameworks.method.shared.text.message: The form's JSON document, rules, behaviour, step flow and fake API are shared by the three stacks; the component registry and the page entry differ. The measurement scenarios are those of the form-library report; they follow one DOM contract of the kits and pick list options through the library's driver.

benchmark.frameworks.method.parity.text.message: Before measuring, Playwright runs {n} cross-e2e scenarios on the same prod builds: errors, server checks, masks, the wizard, arrays and the canonical payload. Measuring starts only after a green run.

benchmark.frameworks.method.remount.text.message: Each mount creates a new framework root with the form: createRoot in React, createApp in Vue, createComponent in Angular. The component library is set up once per page (a Vuetify instance, Taiga UI providers). The form is built after the initial values load — compare “mount until ready”.

benchmark.frameworks.method.stats.text.message: Each run is reduced (for example, the median over all keys of a phase); over {runs} runs come the median and the interquartile range. There is no significance and no “best” mark in a row: with different component libraries a ranking would read as a ranking of frameworks, which this measurement does not show.

benchmark.frameworks.method.renders.text.message: In the form-library report renders are counted by the React DevTools hook; Vue and Angular have no such counter, so this report has no renders section.

benchmark.frameworks.method.cdp.text.message: “JS execution (CDP)” and “JS per key” come from the ScriptDuration counter of the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and it does not count code in promise reactions (Promise.then). Vue re-renders in Promise.then, so these rows understate Vue several times over and are not comparable with the other stacks; they are left out of the key results. Input and click latencies, Total Blocking Time and layout do not have this error.

benchmark.frameworks.method.limits.text.message: CPU throttling in Chromium slows only the main thread — the cost of large bundles is understated. One machine and one browser; absolute numbers from different sessions are not comparable, compare the stacks within the report: in a run they alternate in shuffled order. Neighbouring processes are not sampled on Windows — the “foreign load” column is empty.

homepage.ecosystem.cdk.p3.message: Zero CSS: made for your company's design system

homepage.ecosystem.uikit.p2.message: Masks, OTP codes, dates, combobox, file upload, step wizard and arrays

homepage.ecosystem.uikit.p3.message: A field goes into the schema as is, and onto the screen in one line

homepage.ecosystem.mcp.title.message: Your AI assistant writes forms from the docs, not by guessing

homepage.ecosystem.mcp.p1.message: Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients get docs and examples right in the conversation

homepage.builder.title.message: Build a form with the mouse — or just ask the AI

homepage.builder.lead.message: A visual form builder: assemble a form from kit components, see it live right away and export it as code — a ready module for your React app.

homepage.builder.note.message: Requires a Chromium-based browser: Chrome, Edge, Arc or Brave.

homepage.builder.shotAlt.message: The builder: the form tree and the assistant panel — asked to “Add a Phone field”, the assistant added the field and updated the module code

homepage.builder.caption.message: One assistant turn: the field is added and the form module code is updated

homepage.builder.ai.title.message: The AI assistant edits the form on request

homepage.builder.ai.text.message: “Add an email field”, “make the phone required”, “split the form into three steps”. Every turn can be undone as a whole.

homepage.builder.model.text.message: Anthropic or OpenAI with an API key, or a local one: Ollama, LM Studio.

homepage.builder.noBackend.text.message: The builder runs entirely in the browser: it opens the project folder straight from disk and saves back to it. Model requests go from the browser too — there is no backend to deploy.

homepage.builder.plugins.text.message: The file tree, editors, preview, code generation and the assistant are plugins themselves. Your own plugin can add a panel, a command, an editor, a component kit or a tool for the assistant.

homepage.builder.config.text.message: The .ui_builder/ folder sets the title, language and theme, the plugin set, the default kit, form templates and code printing templates.

homepage.builder.code.text.message: Export prints a TypeScript form module: schema, model, rules, behavior, page. Edits go into the same JSON form file that lives in your repository.

homepage.why.title.message: One standard for every form in the project

homepage.why.lead.message: A form is values, rules, reactions to input, steps and submission. ReFormer gives them one way of writing. That brings readable code, easy review and maintenance — whoever wrote the form: a person, an AI assistant or the builder.

homepage.why.standard.p1.message: Every form is written the same way: model, schema, rules, behavior

homepage.why.standard.p2.message: Hence readability, less cognitive load and painless review

homepage.why.standard.p3.message: The MCP server and the builder write to the same standard

homepage.why.developer.title.message: No useEffect chains, no extra re-renders

homepage.why.developer.p1.message: Typing re-renders only its own field

homepage.why.developer.p2.message: Rules, calculations, arrays and steps — declaratively

homepage.why.developer.p3.message: Typed fields and logic tests without React

homepage.why.team.title.message: Every form in the project is built the same way

homepage.why.team.p1.message: A form file is found by its name, not by searching

homepage.why.team.p2.message: A rule change is a diff in one file

homepage.why.team.p3.message: Someone else's form reads like your own

homepage.why.ai.p1.message: The MCP server writes to the same standard

homepage.why.ai.p2.message: “Done” only after a build and a type check

homepage.why.ai.p3.message: {withMcp}% of runs pass the checks against {noMcp}% without MCP, {cost} times cheaper

homepage.why.builder.title.message: The form in the editor, the code in the repo

homepage.why.builder.p1.message: Build it with the mouse or by asking in plain words

homepage.why.builder.p2.message: Export is a plain ReFormer module, not tied to the editor

homepage.why.builder.p3.message: Your own UI kit and your own AI model

homepage.why.platform.title.message: Forms across teams and from the server

homepage.why.platform.p1.message: Micro-frontends: one team registers a form, another mounts it

homepage.why.platform.p2.message: A form from a JSON document — 3.5 times lighter than RJSF in the benchmark

homepage.why.platform.p3.message: Your own design system on top of headless components

homepage.hidden.title.message: What the feature list does not show

homepage.hidden.lead.message: You will not find this in the API: these benefits follow from the standard and the architecture. They are the easiest to miss when choosing a library, and they are the ones that add up over the life of a project.

homepage.hidden.review.text.message: How to lay out a form is settled in advance. Reviews discuss what a change means, not style, and read a diff of one file.

homepage.hidden.architecture.text.message: The model is the single source of truth; data, rules, reactions and the look are separated. The library holds this, not team discipline.

homepage.hidden.flexibility.title.message: Three ways to render, one logic

homepage.hidden.flexibility.text.message: JSX by hand, from the schema or from JSON. The model, rules and behavior stay the same; the way is chosen per form.

homepage.hidden.tokens.text.message: With MCP, creating a form takes about 6 times fewer tokens. Form code is 2–2.5 times shorter — less for the model to read and write.

homepage.hidden.bugs.text.message: Value copies do not diverge, calculations do not loop, a stale check is aborted. These bugs need no tests to catch.

homepage.hidden.merge.text.message: Markup, rules and behavior live in different files. The look, the rules and the fields of one form are edited in parallel.

homepage.hidden.growth.title.message: No dead ends as a form grows

homepage.hidden.growth.text.message: Start with fields in JSX, plug in the renderer, move the schema to JSON or to another bundle — rules and behavior stay.

homepage.hidden.knowledge.title.message: Knowledge does not leave with the author

homepage.hidden.knowledge.text.message: Understand one form and you understand them all. A form whose author has left is maintained by anyone on the team.

homepage.hidden.beyond.text.message: The signal model is also the app store. A form is built over a part of it, so values are not copied back and forth.

diagram.standardEffects.title.message: One form standard and its consequences

diagram.standardEffects.caption.message: A person, MCP and the builder write a form the same way, so the consequences of the standard apply to any form code — whoever wrote it.

diagram.standardEffects.review.sub.message: a change is a one-file diff

diagram.standardEffects.onboarding.sub.message: a file is found by name

diagram.rendererEcosystem.caption.message: The ReFormer core and renderers, framework lanes with their kits, and the tools around them — the MCP server, the AI assistant and the builder. Renderer-JSON draws a document through Renderer-React, and the /neutral entry builds the same document for Vue and Angular. Blocks link to package pages.
